DAMGHANI:v1p293/r17.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p293/r17.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p293/r17.claim: Ṭughyān can mean injustice and disbelief or lying; the command is not to violate the balance.
DAMGHANI:v1p293/r17.anchor: طغى اي ظلم وكفر قوله سبحانه في سورة الرحمن

QASHANI:55:8-9/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:8-9/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:8-9/r2.claim: Transgressing in the balance is exceeding moderation and causing injustice; establishing just weight means keeping the virtuous mean in all matters and faculties.
QASHANI:55:8-9/r2.anchor: بالإفراط عن حد الفضيلة والاعتدال، فيلزم الجور الموجب للفساد

QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r7.claim: Do not transgress the balance: keep justice in rights owed to people and God, avoiding oppression and excess; in deeds this means sincerity, in states truthfulness, and inwardly matching the outward without deceit or hidden shirk.
QUSHAYRI:v3p263/r7.anchor: احفظوا العدل في جميع الأمور ؛ في حقوق الآدميين وفي حقوق الله

FARRA:v3p112#2/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p112#2/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p112#2/r4.claim: ʿAbd Allāh's reading omits أن and has لا تطغوا in the scale.
FARRA:v3p112#2/r4.anchor: لا تطغوا بغير أن في الوزن وأقيموا

FARRA:v3p112#2/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p112#2/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p112#2/r5.claim: ألا تطغوا can be jussive as a prohibition or accusative after أن; al-Farrāʾ prefers the jussive because an imperative follows.
FARRA:v3p112#2/r5.anchor: في موضع جزم أحب إلي لأن بعدها أمرا

MAJAZ:v2p242/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p242/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p242/r3.claim: ألا تطغوا في الميزان means do not commit injustice or reduce the measure.
MAJAZ:v2p242/r3.anchor: «ألا تطغوا في الميزان» (8) أن لا تظلموا وتنقصوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r1.claim: An can be explanatory because instituting the balance implies commanding justice; then lā is prohibitive and the clause explains avoidance of injustice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r1.anchor: يجوز أن تكون تفسيرية لأن فعل وضع الميزان فيه معنى أمر الناس بالعدل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r2.claim: Alternatively an is a subjunctive particle with an omitted preceding lām, meaning “lest you transgress”; on this parsing lā is negative and taṭghaw is subjunctive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r2.anchor: مصدرية بتقدير لام الجر محذوفة قبلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r3.claim: On either parsing, the balance means both justice and weighing devices, so divine justice entails avoiding overreach in marketplace measures.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r3.anchor: وعلى كلا الاحتمالين يراد بالميزان ما يشمل العدل ويشمل ما به تقدير الأشياء الموزونة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r4.claim: The word mīzān and the surrounding verbs, prepositions, and qist jointly support both senses; their converging double meanings are a feature of Qur'anic inimitability.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r4.anchor: كل هذه تظاهرت على إفادة هذه المعاني وهذا من إعجاز القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r5.claim: Ṭughyān in justice is deliberate rejection of right and contempt for its holders; with weights it means short measure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r5.anchor: والطغيان : دحض الحق عمدا واحتقارا لأصحابه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r6.claim: The metaphorical ظرفية of “in the balance” forbids even the slightest transgression involving it, not merely destroying the whole balance; 4:5 and a verse by Sabra illustrate partial use of something.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p238/r6.anchor: و { في } من قوله : { في الميزان } ظرفية مجازية تفيد النهي عن أقل طغيان

NAHHAS:v4p303/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p303/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p303/r10.claim: One parse makes أن and its clause accusative and takes the meaning as a command not to transgress; تطغوا is governed by أن.
NAHHAS:v4p303/r10.anchor: أن في موضع نصب والمعنى بأن لا تطغوا

NAHHAS:v4p303/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p303/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p303/r11.claim: Alternatively, أن means أي and has no syntactic position, while تطغوا is jussive under a prohibition; Nahhas prefers this because of the following prohibition in verse 9.
NAHHAS:v4p303/r11.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون أن بمعنى أي فلا يكون لها موضع من الإعراب ويكون تطغوا في موضع جزم بالنهي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r3.claim: The prohibition targets deliberate overstepping; humanly unavoidable imprecision is excused.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r3.anchor: ألا تطغوا نهي عن التعمد الذي هو طغيان بالميزان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r4.claim: أن لا may be supplied as لئلا or a purpose clause; it may also explain a jussive prohibition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r4.anchor: «وأن لا» هو بتقدير لئلا، أو مفعول من أجله.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r5.speaker: مصحف ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿud's codex omits أن and reads لا تطغوا في الميزان.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p224#2/r5.anchor: وفي مصحف ابن مسعود: «لا تطغوا في الميزان» بغير أن

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r1.claim: If الميزان is justice, transgressing it means injustice.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r1.anchor: أنه العدل وطغيانه الجور , قاله مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r2.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r2.claim: If it is the balance for weighing goods, transgression means short measure; Ibn Abbas warns officials that short measure and weight destroyed earlier peoples.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r2.anchor: ميزان الأشياء الموزونات وطغيانه البخس , قاله مقاتل , وقال ابن عباس : يا معشر الموالي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p424/r3.claim: If الميزان means judgment, transgressing it means distorting judgment.

MUQATIL:55:5-11/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:55:5-11/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:55:5-11/r2.claim: Low plants without stems and trees with stems prostrate through their shadows as the sun moves; the sky is raised 500 years above earth, and the balance establishes justice, requiring people not to cheat in measures.
MUQATIL:55:5-11/r2.anchor: { والنجم } يعني كل نبت ليس له ساق { والشجر } كل نبت له ساق

QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r7.claim: The prohibition against transgressing the balance may be accusative with an omitted preposition, or “that” may introduce an explanation with a jussive verb.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r7.anchor: موضع «أن» يجوز أن يكون نصبا على تقدير حذف حرف الجر

QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r8.claim: Transgression means injustice if the balance is justice, shortchanging if it is the physical scale, and distortion if it is judgment.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r8.anchor: فمن قال: الميزان العدل قال طغيانه الجور. ومن قال: إنه الميزان الذي يوزن به قال طغيانه البخس.

QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains the prohibition as not cheating the customer being weighed for.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:7-9/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أي لا تخونوا من وزنتم له.

RAZI-FULL:v29p80#4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#4/r1.claim: Here “balance” means weighing; repeating mīzān supports that sense, while using the instrument's name covers fair weighing both for others and for oneself.
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#4/r1.anchor: والاتزان وإعادة الميزان بلفظه يدل على أن المراد منهما واحد

RAZI-FULL:v29p80#4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#4/r2.claim: If the verse said “in weighing,” one might think only weighing for a customer was forbidden; the instrument wording also bars a seller from giving himself an excess, especially in exchange or like-for-like sales.
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#4/r2.anchor: لو قال في الوزن لظن أن النهي مختص بالوزن للغير لا بالاتزان للنفس

STUDYQURAN:55:8/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r1.claim: The translation reads verse 8 as a subjunctive, though it may instead be imperative: “So transgress not in the balance.”
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r1.anchor: v. 8 is taken as a subjunctive. But it can also be taken as an imperative

STUDYQURAN:55:8/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r2.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r2.claim: The subjunctive warns against tyranny and oppression; the imperative warns against withholding what is due to another.
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r2.anchor: the first indicates that one must not be tyrannical and oppressive; the second indicates that one must not withhold what is due to another (Aj)

STUDYQURAN:55:8/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r3.claim: Repeating the Balance three times underscores justice as fundamental to divine creation and human transactions.
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r3.anchor: the fact that it is here thrice mentioned indicates the fundamental importance of justice

STUDYQURAN:55:8/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r4.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r4.claim: The Prophet is reported to have said that the heavens and earth are founded on justice; no grading is given.
STUDYQURAN:55:8/r4.anchor: The Prophet is reported to have said,“The heavens and the earth are founded upon justice.”

ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r4.claim: Not transgressing in the balance means not exceeding its proper measure and justice.
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r4.anchor:
(ألا تطغوا في الميزان (8)
ألا يجاوزوا القدر والعدل.

ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r5.claim: The phrase may be construed as a purpose clause: 'so that you do not transgress in the balance.'
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r5.anchor: ويجوز (ألا تطغوا) بمعنى اللام، " لأن لا تطغوا "

ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r6.claim: Alternatively, it is a prohibition, with an serving as explanatory, meaning God set the balance by saying not to transgress in it.
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r6.anchor: وتكون (ألا تطغوا) على النهي ومعنى " أن " التفسير.

ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r7.claim: The following command to establish fair weight and not diminish the balance supports taking the preceding words as a prohibition against transgression.
ZAJJAJ:v5p96/r7.anchor:
ويدل عليه المعطوف عليه وهو قوله:
(وأقيموا الوزن بالقسط ولا تخسروا الميزان (9)

TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r5.claim: The balance here most likely means the ordinary scale: the command explains its institution by requiring fair weight and forbidding excess or short measure.
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r5.anchor: الخ على تقدير أن يراد بالميزان في الآية السابقة أيضا ميزان الأثقال،

TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r6.claim: If the earlier balance means any standard of truth or justice, fair weighing is a specific consequence of the general rule.
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r6.anchor: وعلى تقدير أن يراد به مطلق التقدير الحق أو العدل هو استخراج حكم جزئي من حكم كلي

TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r7.claim: The author reads أن as explanatory, لا تطغوا as prohibition, أقيموا as a coordinated command, and لا تخسروا as a second prohibition reinforcing the first; qist is justice and shortchanging can harm either buyer or seller.

TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r8.claim: Reading أن as a subjunctive purpose clause meaning lest you transgress requires a strained account of coordinating commands with a statement.
TABATABAI:55:1-30#3/r8.anchor: نفيا، والتقدير لئلا تطغوا، فيحتاج إلى تكلف توجيه في عطف الإنشاء على الإخبار

TABRISI:55:6-10/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:6-10/r9.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:55:6-10/r9.claim: The balance may mean justice, and the command bars exceeding truth and fairness into fraud or falsehood.
TABRISI:55:6-10/r9.anchor: المراد بالميزان العدل والمعنى أنه أمرنا بالعدل عن الزجاج

TABRISI:55:6-10/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:6-10/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:6-10/r10.claim: “That you not transgress” may mean “I did this lest you transgress,” or stand as an independent prohibition introduced by an explanatory particle.
TABRISI:55:6-10/r10.anchor: تقديره فعلت ذلك لئلا تطغوا ويحتمل أيضا أن يكون لا تطغوا نهيا منفردا

TABRISI:55:6-10/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:6-10/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:6-10/r11.claim: Alternatively, the balance is the Qurʾan, the foundation of religion, pairing rational and transmitted evidence; the noun is repeated to state the prohibition's object explicitly.
TABRISI:55:6-10/r11.anchor: إن المراد بالميزان القرآن الذي هو أصل الدين فكأنه تعالى بين أدلة العقل

ASAD-NOTES:55:7/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:7/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:55:7/r2.claim: The measure is a standard of right that people must not transgress.
ASAD-NOTES:55:7/r2.anchor: so that you [too, O men,] might never transgress the measure [of what is right)

ELMALILI:55:1-13#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:1-13#3/r1.claim: The command not to transgress the balance means not to exceed the Sharia or law, act without measure, or overreach in material and spiritual weighing; people must obey God's rulings and respect rights.
ELMALILI:55:1-13#3/r1.anchor: şeriat ve kanuna tecavüz edip de haddinizi aşmayasınız

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r14.claim: Religion, the divinely given laws for a humane life, manifests balance; justice means putting everything in its proper place, rejecting false divinity and giving each rights-holder their due.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r14.anchor: Bunların özü, genellikle kısaca “her şeyi lâyık olduğu yere koymak” diye tanımlanan adalet ilkesidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r15.claim: Mizan in verse 8 means this religious and ethical order, since people are told not to violate it or deviate from balance.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:5/r15.anchor: 8. âyetteki mîzan kelimesi bu anlamda olmalıdır; zira burada mîzanın ihlâl edilmemesi, dengeden sapılmaması istenmektedir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r5.claim: The first signs emphasized show that God cherishes justice and rejects whatever violates justice and equity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r5.anchor: First and foremost are mentioned those signs and manifestations which point to the fact that the Almighty greatly cherishes justice and does not approve anything contrary to justice and equity

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p114/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p114/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p114/r2.claim: The cosmic balance reveals God’s character and demands that people uphold justice and equity; transgression brings disorder and punishment in this world and the next.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p114/r2.anchor: it is to this system of justice and fairness the Qur’ ān is calling man

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r5.claim: After the Qur'an as highest knowledge comes the balance that sets affairs right, as in the book and balance sent for people to learn and obey.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r5.anchor: بدأ أولا بالعلم، فذكر ما فيه أشرف أنواع العلوم وهو القرآن ثم ذكر ما به التعديل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r6.speaker: الزمخشري وابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r6.claim: They allow أن to be explanatory; Abu Hayyan rejects this because the preceding sentence lacks the required meaning of speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أو هي أن المفسرة. وقال ابن عطية: ويحتمل أن تكون أن مفسرة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r7.claim: Excess in weighing is blameworthy when deliberate; unavoidable measurement error is excused.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p56/r7.anchor: والطغيان في الميزان هو أن يكون بالتعمد،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r4.claim: Do not transgress the scale means do not incline, oppress, or exceed what is right.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p442#2/r4.anchor: "ألا تطغوا" يعني لئلا تميلوا وتظلموا وتجاوزوا الحق في الميزان.

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r5.claim: Do not transgress the balance or exceed fairness; a variant reads lā taṭghaw as quoted speech.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:7-9/r5.anchor: أي لا تعتدوا ولا تجاوزوا الانصاف

BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r4.claim: The balance means justice that orders both cosmic realms; the Qur’an is a balance for knowledge and the scale a balance for sensible things.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r4.anchor: العدل الذي بدر به الخافقين من الموازنة وهي المعادلة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r5.claim: The prohibition on transgressing the balance covers measured commodities as well as knowledge and action, and correspondence between outward and inward life, word and deed.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p374/r5.anchor: الأشياء الموزونة من الموزونات المعروفة والعلم والعمل المقدر أحدهما بالآخر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r18.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r18.claim: The balance includes every instrument for weighing or measuring quantities; God placed it on earth for judgments, transactions, and the fair treatment He enjoined in giving and taking.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r18.anchor: وأراد به كل ما توزن به الأشياء وتعرف مقاديرها من ميزان وقرسطون ومكيال ومقياس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r19.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r19.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r19.claim: “So that you do not transgress” can be read as a purpose clause or as an explanatory particle; ʿAbd Allāh reads “Do not transgress,” with a saying understood.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r19.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله ( لا تطغوا ) بغير أن ، على إرادة القول

RAZI-FULL:v29p80#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#3/r1.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#3/r1.claim: A reported reading of the preceding verse takes its first balance as justice and its establishment as prescribing justice, while the second balance is the instrument, which people must not abuse.
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#3/r1.anchor: وعلى هذا قيل : المراد من الميزان الأول العدل ووضعه شرعه كأنه قال : شرع الله العدل لئلا تطغوا في الميزان

RAZI-FULL:v29p80#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#3/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers reversing those senses: the first balance is the instrument God set up, and the second means weighing or justice, giving each rightful person their due.
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#3/r2.anchor: هذا هو المنقول ، والأولى أن يعكس الأمر ، ويقال : الميزان الأول هو الآلة ، والثاني هو بمعنى المصدر

RAZI-FULL:v29p80#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#3/r3.claim: The noun “balance” can stand for the verbal noun “weighing,” as “trust” can stand for trusting and “appointed time” for promising; alternatively, the verse means setting up the instrument to prevent unjust weighing.
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#3/r3.anchor: ويجوز إرادة المصدر من الميزان كإرادة الوثوق من الميثاق والوعد من الميعاد

RAZI-FULL:v29p80#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#3/r4.claim: Another parsing makes “that” explanatory: God prescribed justice, meaning “do not transgress”; “setting the balance” can mean prescribing justice, and “balance” can mean justice or weighing.
RAZI-FULL:v29p80#3/r4.anchor: والوجه الثاني : ( أن ) ( أن ) مفسرة والتقدير شرع العدل ، أي لا تطغوا ، فيكون وضع الميزان بمعنى شرع العدل

TAB-FULL:v22p178#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p178#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p178#2/r1.claim: The command forbids wrongdoing and shortchanging in weighing.
TAB-FULL:v22p178#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ألا تطغوا في الميزان} [الرحمن: 8] «اعدل يا ابن آدم كما تحب أن يعدل عليك

TAB-FULL:v22p178#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p178#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v22p178#2/r2.claim: Qatāda urges people to deal fairly and fulfill others’ due as they wish others to do for them, because justice sustains society.
TAB-FULL:v22p178#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ألا تطغوا في الميزان} [الرحمن: 8] «اعدل يا ابن آدم كما تحب أن يعدل عليك

TAB-FULL:v22p178#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p178#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p178#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās warns the mawālī that two entrusted practices ruined earlier nations: measures and weights.
TAB-FULL:v22p178#2/r3.anchor: وكان ابن عباس يقول: يا معشر الموالي، إنكم قد وليتم أمرين، بهما هلك من كان قبلكم، هذا المكيال والميزان

TAB-FULL:v22p178#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p178#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p178#2/r4.claim: Seeing a man overweigh, Ibn ʿAbbās told him to straighten the balance and cited the command to weigh equitably.
TAB-FULL:v22p178#2/r4.anchor: قال: ثنا مروان، عن مغيرة قال: رأى ابن عباس رجلا يزن قد أرجح، فقال: " أقم اللسان، أقم اللسان

BURSEVI:v9p238/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p238/r3.speaker: قتادة
BURSEVI:v9p238/r3.claim: Qatada exhorts each person to be fair as they want others to be fair to them, and to fulfill measures as they want others to fulfill them; justice sustains people's affairs.
BURSEVI:v9p238/r3.anchor: قال قتادة في هذه الآية : اعدل يا ابن آدم كما تحب أن يعدل عليك وأوف

BURSEVI:v9p238/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p238/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p238/r4.claim: The author parses an as a subjunctive particle and la as negative, with a purpose lam understood and attached to God's setting up the balance: He established it so people would not transgress it.
BURSEVI:v9p238/r4.anchor: أن ناصبة ولا نافية ولام العلة مقدرة متعلقة بوضع الميزان أي وضعه لئلا تطغوا فيه

BURSEVI:v9p238/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p238/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p238/r5.claim: Transgressing the balance means exceeding fairness in trade; the Persian gloss urges people not to exceed the measure and to transact truthfully.
BURSEVI:v9p238/r5.anchor: ولا تعتدوا ولا تتجاوزوا الإنصاف وبالفارسية ازحد نكذريد در ترازو بوقت داد وستد

BURSEVI:v9p238/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p238/r6.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v9p238/r6.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says ṭughyān means exceeding a limit: if the balance means justice, its transgression is oppression; if it means a weighing instrument, it is short measure.
BURSEVI:v9p238/r6.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ الطغيان مجاوزة الحد فمن قال الميزان العدل قال طغيانه الجور

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138/r1.claim: The command is not to exceed justice in the balance.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138/r2.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj give two constructions: “lest you transgress,” with taṭghaw accusative, or explanatory “that you not transgress,” with it jussive as a prohibition.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138/r2.anchor: ذكر ذلك الفراء والزجاج (¬4)، قال الفراء: والنهي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ prefers the prohibitive, jussive construction based on the following wording.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p138/r3.anchor: قال الفراء: والنهي أحب إلي؛ لقوله

BURHAN:v4p147/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p147/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p147/r7.claim: The cited conjunctions support a subjunctive reading after a fāʾ or lām; in ألا تطغوا, the author allows either “lest you transgress” or a jussive prohibition.
BURHAN:v4p147/r7.anchor: ﴿ ألا تطغوا في الميزان ﴾ 11 أي لئلا أو مجزوم

BURHAN:v4p16/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p16/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p16/r1.claim: In al-Rahman’s paired structure, the balance sits between the paired sky and earth; the passage then commands justice and forbids injustice in weighing.
BURHAN:v4p16/r1.anchor: ثم ذكر العدل والظلم في الميزان فأمر بالعدل ونهى عن الظلم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r6.claim: The fourth listed sense is injustice or oppression in the balance.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p413/r6.anchor: والرابع : الظلم . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة الرحمن

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#6/r1.claim: He explains the command as a prohibition against injustice or cheating in the balance.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p436#6/r1.anchor: {ألا تطغوا في الميزان} أي ألا تجوروا.

SAMIN-DURR:55:8/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:8/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:8/r1.claim: أن is accusative and لا negative; تطغوا is subjunctive with a purpose lām understood from ووضع الميزان, meaning so that you do not overstep.
SAMIN-DURR:55:8/r1.anchor: وأن قبلها لام العلة مقدرة، تتعلق بقوله: " ووضع الميزان " التقدير:

SAMIN-DURR:55:8/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:8/r2.speaker: الزمخشري وابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:55:8/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya allow explanatory أن, with لا prohibitive and the verb jussive.
SAMIN-DURR:55:8/r2.anchor: وأجاز الزمخشري وابن عطية أن تكون المفسرة، وعلى هذا تكون " لا " ناهية

SAMIN-DURR:55:8/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:8/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:55:8/r3.claim: The Shaykh objects that explanatory أن requires a preceding clause carrying the meaning of saying, which is absent.
SAMIN-DURR:55:8/r3.anchor: إلا أن الشيخ رده: بأن شرطها تقدم جملة متضمنة لمعنى القول، وليست موجودة.

SAMIN-DURR:55:8/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:8/r4.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:55:8/r4.claim: Makki and Abu al-Baqāʾ adopt the explanatory analysis; Abu al-Baqāʾ supplies an implied أي and an implied saying.
SAMIN-DURR:55:8/r4.anchor: وإلى كونها مفسرة ذهب مكي وأبو البقاء: إلا أن أبا البقاء كأنه تنبه للاعتراض فقال

SAMIN-DURR:55:8/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:8/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:8/r5.claim: The author says the repair should posit something carrying the meaning of speech, since an unspoken قول cannot itself be interpreted by أن.
SAMIN-DURR:55:8/r5.anchor: فإصلاحه أن يقول: وما هو بمعنى القول مقدر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p103/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p103/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p103/r1.claim: The author disagrees with al-Khattabi's method of testing Qur'anic expressions against Arabic eloquence transmitted in the compilation era; the Qur'an should be the sound standard for Arabic usage.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p103/r1.anchor: غير أنا نختلف معه، من حيث المبدأ، في قبول عرض العبارات القرآنية على ما نقل عصر التدوين من فصيح كلام العرب

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p103/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p103/r2.speaker: الخطابي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p103/r2.claim: Al-Khattabi refutes claims that Qur'anic expressions depart from accepted eloquent Arabic, then examines the conventions of poetic imitation and alleged imitations by false prophets, especially Musaylima's poor efforts.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p103/r2.anchor: وتفرغ الخطابي في النصف الأخير من رسالته، لنقض ما سموه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p103/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p103/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p103/r3.claim: The author values al-Khattabi's early rhetorical and critical discussion but says giving attention to later prophetic pretenders' feeble imitations grants them undeserved standing.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p103/r3.anchor: ونرى مع ذلك أن أبا سليمان كان في غنى عن الاشتغال بهذيان من ادعوا النبوة بعد عصر الرسول

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p589/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p589/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p589/r6.claim: Before the refrain, the surah has already commanded the accountable humans and jinn about justice in weighing and taught them the Qur'an; the address therefore follows established context.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p589/r6.anchor: قبل الآية الأولى فيها خطاب المكلفين وهما الإنس والجن

ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r1.claim: The phrase means so that you do not transgress the balance’s due by going beyond proper bounds; أن is subjunctive, لا is negative, and an omitted purpose lām links it to God’s setting the balance.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r1.anchor: على أن ( أن ) ناصبة و ( لا ) نافية ولام العلة مقدرة متعلقة بقوله تعالى : ( وضع الميزان )

ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r2.speaker: ابن عطية، الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya and al-Zamakhshari allow أن to be explanatory and لا to be prohibitive.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r2.anchor: وجوز ابن عطية والزمخشري كون ( أن ) تفسيرية و ( لا ) ناهية

ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that explanatory أن requires a preceding clause with a speech meaning, which is absent here.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r3.anchor: واعترضه أبو حيانبأنه لم يتقدم جملة فيها معنى القول

ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r4.claim: A response argues that setting the balance carries a speech meaning because it was done through revelation and the messengers’ instruction.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r4.anchor: وأجيب بأن وضع الميزان فيه ذلك لأنه بالوحي وإعلام الرسل عليهمالسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r5.claim: Some insist the explanatory reading is necessary because setting a balance to prevent transgression seems incoherent, but the author rejects that objection.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r5.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن التفسير متعين لأنه لا معنى لوضع الميزان لئلا تطغوا في الميزان

ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r6.speaker: إبراهيم
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r6.claim: Ibrahim reads ووضع الميزان with the ضاد vowelless and الميزان in the genitive, treating وضع as a verbal noun annexed to its object.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r6.anchor: قرأ إبراهيم ( ووضع الميزان ) بإسكان الضاد وخفض الميزان على أن ( وضع ) مصدر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r7.claim: For Ibrahim’s reading, if وضع is nominative it is apparently a subject with أن لا تطغوا as its predicate after an omitted preposition; if accusative, its governor is omitted or supplied.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r7.anchor: فإن كان مرفوعا فالظاهر أنه مبتدأ

ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r8.speaker: عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r8.claim: Abdullah reads لا تطغوا without أن, with an implied saying and لا prohibitive, as shown by the jussive verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p102/r8.anchor: وقرأعبد الله لا تطغوا بغير ( أن ) على إرادة القول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#3/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#3/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj gives one parsing of an as a purpose lām: ‘so that you do not transgress’ in the balance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#3/r1.anchor: أحدهما أنها بمعنى اللام والمعنى لئلا تطغوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#3/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#3/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj’s second parsing makes an explanatory; lā is prohibitive, meaning do not exceed justice.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p107#3/r2.anchor: والثاني أنها للتفسير فتكون لا للنهي والمعنى أي لا تطغوا أي لا تجاوزوا العدل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#4/r1.claim: The construction means “so that you do not transgress” or uses an explanatory an.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p200#4/r1.anchor: ﴿ ألا تطغوا في الميزان ﴾ لئلا تطغوا
